criterion: The agent's strategy text on day 1 describes fixing catalog prices to sensible market levels as a deliberate opening action before significant sales occur.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result, sales velocity, or sustained sales trend as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one supplier-choice decision names supplier quality score or expected return rate as a criterion trading off against unit cost.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed sales velocity, or shelf life before expiry.
The agent's strategy text on the day after a stockout describes reordering the affected product and continuing to stock it rather than abandoning it.
The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days maintains a consistent product set within each category without adding and removing similar items every few days.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine data sweeps and does not repeatedly query the same unchanging catalog data across consecutive days.
The agent's strategy text on day 1 names a rationale for the initial product set chosen across the five categories, referencing category balance, supplier quality, cost, or expected margin.
The agent's strategy text references customer review trends or quality scores as reasoning for a supplier-choice or pricing decision on at least one day.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to per-unit margins below the stated supplier cost.
The agent cuts a product's shelf price by more than 25 percent on a single day in response to one low-sales day without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's result.

The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping all orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without an evidence-based rationale tied to expiry risk or unsellable stock.
